== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' was baptised at Irvine, Ayrshire, on 03 Feb 1723. The parish register names his father as [[Glasgow-4164|James Glasgow]] and his mother as [[Rae-3515|Marion Rae]].<ref name="FMP1" /> Because the entry records a baptism rather than a birth, his birth is placed before that date, and Irvine is inferred from the baptism rather than independently recorded.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-4158]] is assessed at 97% (proved). William’s 3 February 1723 Irvine transcript names James Glasgow and Marion Rae. Father-4158 absorbed the separate 4164 account and explicitly represents both the 1721 Margt and 1723 Marion entries; shared father/parish and close chronology favour one adult father, with the maternal-name distinction unresolved.

Recorded father James is near99%;97% includes consolidation with the 1721 Rae-household father while keeping Margaret and Marion wording distinct.

Next useful test: Compare original 1721 and 1723 entries for trade, residence and the two maternal given names.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3573825&tab=this Findmypast transcript (), Archive reference: OPR 595/1; Baptism date: 03 Feb 1723; Baptism year: 1723; Category: Birth, Marriage, Death & Parish Records; Collections from: Great Britain, Scotland; Country: Scotland; County: Ayrshire; Father's]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


The baptism is the only record found for William Glasgow. A search of live WikiTree profiles found no compatible match; [[Glasgow-3962|William]] belongs to a different family and is not this person.

=== Possible William Glascoe / Glascow, 1760 defendant ===
William Glascoe is among prisoners reported sentenced to transportation after Old Bailey trials, for stealing a sack of malt from a warehouse, valued in the newspaper at £4 10s.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/35690357/ Public Ledger or Daily Register of Commerce and Intelligence, 1760-04-18, p.2].</ref>

The newspaper uses Glascoe; the associated Old Bailey case uses Glascow. The case association does not establish the defendant’s origin, family or identity with the later Maryland man.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4120]]. The recorded before 1723-02-03 birth at Irvine, Ayrshire, Scotland is chronologically compatible. The newspaper gives no family or individual identifier connecting this occurrence to Glasgow-4120.

=== Possible William Glasgow, master of the Lady Forbes ===
William Glasgow is named as master of the Lady Forbes in the Sutton shipping casualty report.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050136699/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1768-01-23, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395700744/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1768-02-06, p.2].</ref>

The January 1768 report says the rum-carrying Lady Forbes, bound for Waterford, was driven ashore near Sutton and the crew were saved. The ship’s Glasgow home port does not give William’s birthplace. No identity with the later brig William or Falmouth master follows.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4120]]. Birth before 3 February 1723; Irvine baptism. Chronologically compatible, but no master, vessel or maritime identification.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Philadelphia and Charles-Town postal lists, 1759–1771 ===
William Glasgow, Cecil County, is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39399295/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1759-08-09, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in February 1763.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39390517/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1763-02-24, p.1].</ref>

William Glasgow is listed among letters remaining in the Philadelphia post office in October 1765.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39405824/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1765-10-10, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is separately listed in the Charles-Town, Maryland, post-office letters notice headed 1 October 1771, beside an entry for John Glasgow of West Nottingham.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41041559/ Maryland Gazette, 1771-10-24, p.3].</ref>

Cecil County explicitly qualifies the 1759 entry only. In 1763 "Pennsylvania" follows James Gillispie; in 1765 "Forks of Delaware" qualifies William Greenlee, not William Glasgow. The entries may concern different men, and co-listing with John in 1771 does not prove a family relationship.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4120]]. Birth before 3 February 1723, Irvine, permits these dates; no postal identification.
